title: Deployment corridor ops journal - VPC/on-prem blockers & next steps
body:
Context and purpose:
This is a lightweight, human-facing journal for the week focused on the "deployment corridor"—the set of customer installs that are high-touch, multi-site, or have active network/security blockers. The goal is to capture what we observed in standups, the hard blockers, short-term mitigations, and owners for next steps. Use this to orient cross-functional responders before the daily triage.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Three active installs showing elevated post-install networking flakiness (two VPC customers, one on-prem air-gapped).
- Primary root causes: MTU/path-MTU mismatches + stateful firewall session timeouts + an unexpected kubelet conntrack limit on one appliance image.
- Short-term mitigations implemented this week: MTU clamp snippets, keepalive tuning for our sidecar, and a kernel conntrack patch on image v2026.07.2.
- Owners assigned for customer escalations (see action tracker).

Sync log (chronological highlights):
2026-07-20 09:15 - Standup (field-ops + network SRE + install eng)
- Customer A (large fintech, VPC): intermittent token streaming truncation at ~12–20s into stream. Observed packet fragmentation and retransmits on the path to the dedicated pool. Slack thread: #pd-field-ops.
- Customer B (healthcare, on-prem): deployment passes smoke checks but fails sustained load due to kubelet dropping connections when ephemeral port exhaustion occurs.
- Customer C (e-commerce, VPC): TLS re-handshake failures with a third-party proxy; suspicion of middlebox deep-packet-inspection (DPI) interfering with longer-lived sockets.

2026-07-20 14:00 - Deep-dive with network SRE (Julian + Ethan)
- Replayed pcap from Customer A: MSS advertised by upstream was too large; fragmentation caused out-of-order arrival and gRPC stream decode errors. Action: push MTU clamp as a configurable install-time flag in the installer (Priya).
- Customer B: reproduced port exhaustion in a small lab with accelerated session churn. Root cause in appliance image: default conntrack max too low for 10k ephemeral sockets per minute. Action: publish hotfix image v2026.07.2 (Sanaa).

2026-07-21 10:30 - Customer A war room
- Applied MTU clamp (1500 -> 1400) at customer edge with immediate improvement in p95 latency for streaming. Still seeing rare truncation; file capture will be collected during next spike. Owner: Ethan.

2026-07-21 16:00 - Install retro (internal)
- Noted gaps in install checklist: we did not validate path MTU for customers with shared transit providers. Proposal: add a path-MTU probe step and vendor-specific notes to the runbook. Owner: Maya.

Issue highlights (detailed):
1) Packet fragmentation & streaming truncation (Customer A)
- Symptoms: gRPC streams cut around 12–20s and client-side resumes are inconsistent.
- Hypothesis: large initial MSS + middlebox path causing fragmentation and retransmits.
- Action taken: MTU clamp flag tested; installer change request #502 opened.
- Next steps: schedule 2-hour window during low traffic to run continuous pcap capture; target date 2026-07-25. Owner: Ethan.

2) Conntrack/ephemeral port exhaustion (Customer B)
- Symptoms: node kubelet logs spike with 'connection reset' and OOM-killer like symptoms for kube-proxy on heavy churn.
- Root cause: conntrack max default on our appliance image too conservative for customer traffic profile.
- Action taken: hotfix image built and smoke-tested in staging (v2026.07.2).
- Next steps: roll hotfix to Customer B on 2026-07-22 with rollback plan; instrument conntrack metrics in the console for any future rollouts. Owner: Sanaa.

3) TLS re-handshake / DPI interference (Customer C)
- Symptoms: periodic TLS handshake failures when long-lived sessions are negotiated through third-party proxy.
- Investigation notes: proxy vendor (XProxy) has a known DPI signature that forces re-key; vendor patch cadence unclear.
- Workaround: enable TLS session tickets and reduce re-key frequency where policy allows; legal/security sign-off required for ticket persistence.
- Owner: Julian (legal loop-in: Priya).

Action tracker (short):
- Priya: add path-MTU probe and vendor addenda to onprem-runbook-v2 (target 2026-07-28).
- Ethan: continuous pcap window for Customer A (target 2026-07-25).
- Sanaa: roll hotfix image to Customer B with staged canary (target 2026-07-22).
- Maya: create a runbook checklist item for 'verify conntrack & ephemeral port table size' and add dashboard alert (target 2026-07-24).
- Julian: vendor escalation for XProxy and produce a recommended config snippet for customers (target 2026-07-29).

Known risks & questions:
- Risk: Installer change to default MTU behavior increases complexity for low-touch installs; need clear opt-in/opt-out semantics.
- Risk: Hotfix image must pass compliance scan for healthcare customer (Customer B); security scan backlog could delay rollout.
- Question: Should we make conntrack tuning a permanent part of appliance images for all customers, or keep it per-customer? Tradeoffs: stability vs unexpected side effects on low-traffic sites.

Short-term mitigations applied this week (operational summary):
- MTU clamp flag pushed to a branch in deploy-scripts; test harness added for on-the-wire verification.
- Keepalive and application-level heartbeat added to streaming sidecar (reduces session teardown probability on flaky middleboxes).
- Hotfix image published and smoke-tested in staging; integration tests added to preflight pipeline.

Communication notes for CS and Solutions Engineering:
- Customer A: share post-mitigation summary and propose a 2-hour capture window; provide clear rollback plan. (CS owner: Priya)
- Customer B: coordinate a maintenance window and compliance sign-off; provide staging evidence of fixes. (SE owner: Julian)
- Customer C: request vendor configuration and offer alternate routing options if vendor cannot commit. (CS owner: Ethan)

Follow-ups for next week
- Confirm MTU clamp installer knob UX and communicate to low-touch installs team.
- Finalize conntrack instrumentation dashboards and alert thresholds.
- Run a small internal chaos test for session churn scenarios to validate conntrack defaults across appliance SKUs.

Appendix (quick references):
- Runbook link: Confluence: /deployments/private/onprem-runbook-v2
- Installer change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-scripts/pull/502
- Hotfix image: registry.redwood.ai/appliance:v2026.07.2
- Related Jira: PD-1987 (Customer A streaming truncation), PD-2011 (Customer B conntrack hotfix)

Notes to self (freeform):
- Consider adding a 'corridor' tag to the console so we can filter runs that are high-touch vs low-touch. Helps with capacity planning for field teams.
- Keep a short list of common middleboxes (vendors + signatures) in the runbook so on-call doesn't have to re-discover DPI issues each time.

---
If anything in this journal needs expansion into a PRD or a longer retro, ping me (Maya) and I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up.
